edges.reason: msg.sender is stored into the owner state variable inside the Ownable constructor.
The Ownable constructor derives ownership directly from the caller-controlled msg.sender.
transfer reads and debits balances[msg.sender], making the caller the implicit source of funds.
transferFrom validates allowed[_from][msg.sender] against the caller identity.
approve writes the allowance for allowed[msg.sender][_spender].
transferOwnership is gated by the onlyOwner check evaluated on msg.sender.
freedWosPoolForSecondStage is owner-gated and credits balances[msg.sender].
freedWosPoolForThirdStage is owner-gated and credits balances[msg.sender].
freedWosPoolToTeam is owner-gated and credits balances[msg.sender].
freedWosPoolToWosSystem is owner-gated and credits balances[msg.sender].
block.timestamp feeds the deadline comparison that authorizes the team pool release.
deadlineToFreedTeamPool is read by the time-based release gate.
The outcome of freedWosPoolToTeam depends on the miner-influenceable block.timestamp.
transfer mutates the balances mapping using SafeMath sub/add.
transferFrom reads and decrements allowed[_from][msg.sender].
transferFrom moves value between balances entries.
approve overwrites the allowed mapping entry for the spender.
INITIAL_SUPPLY is assigned to totalSupply in the WOS constructor.
The constructor reads INITIAL_SUPPLY to derive total supply and pool allocations.
totalSupply is divided and multiplied to compute peerSupply and pool amounts.
peerSupply local is derived from totalSupply.div(100) inside the constructor.
peerSupply flows into the pool allocation multiplications.
Getter returns the wosPoolForSecondStage state variable.
Getter returns the wosPoolForThirdStage state variable.
Getter returns the wosPoolToTeam state variable.
Getter returns the wosPoolToWosSystem state variable.
wosPoolForSecondStage is added to balances[msg.sender] then zeroed.
wosPoolForThirdStage is added to balances[msg.sender] then zeroed.
wosPoolToTeam is added to balances[msg.sender] after the deadline check.
wosPoolToWosSystem is added to balances[msg.sender] then zeroed.
_to parameter is credited with balances[_to].add(_value).
_value parameter drives the subtraction and addition on balances.
_value parameter drives balance and allowance arithmetic in transferFrom.
newOwner parameter is validated and written into the owner state variable.
onlyOwner modifier gates execution of transferOwnership.
onlyOwner modifier gates execution of freedWosPoolForSecondStage.
onlyOwner modifier gates execution of freedWosPoolForThirdStage.
onlyOwner modifier gates execution of freedWosPoolToTeam.
onlyOwner modifier gates execution of freedWosPoolToWosSystem.
Constructor execution reaches the pool allocation arithmetic block.
Constructor invokes SafeMathLib.div to compute peerSupply.
Constructor invokes SafeMathLib.mul for each pool allocation.
Constructor uses SafeMathLib.add to credit balances[msg.sender].
freedWosPoolForSecondStage calls SafeMathLib.add on the caller balance.
freedWosPoolForThirdStage calls SafeMathLib.add on the caller balance.
freedWosPoolToTeam reaches the block.timestamp deadline require statement.
The timestamp check must pass before the team pool addition executes.
Second stage release reaches the pool-to-balance addition operation.
Third stage release reaches the pool-to-balance addition operation.
Team pool release reaches the pool-to-balance addition operation.
System pool release reaches the pool-to-balance addition operation.
Pool addition is executed through SafeMathLib.add despite the redundant inline require.
Pool allocations are computed via SafeMathLib.mul calls.

normalization_plan.reason: The _to parameter only feeds the transfer function body and has no independent role.
The _value parameter only parameterizes the transfer arithmetic.
The _value parameter only parameterizes the transferFrom balance and allowance arithmetic.
newOwner is validated and assigned to the owner state variable inside transferOwnership.
peerSupply exists solely to carry totalSupply/100 into the pool allocation multiplications.
